transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-12
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Record: Yes

Summary: Short demo focused on Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown for Veridian Health's inference workloads. Walked through per-route telemetry, cost attribution, Optimize suggestions (batching, quantization profiles), and initial security questions. Agreed next steps: share TCO spreadsheet, schedule security deep-dive, provision trial org.

Topics: usage analytics, per-route dashboards, route cost allocation, Optimize recommendations, hosted vs dedicated, VPC/SOC2 questions, pilot setup

Action items (captured in transcript and confirmed at end):
- Redwood to share sample cost CSV and TCO spreadsheet (Maya)
- SE to set up 48-hour benchmark run and collect logs (Rohit)
- Security deep-dive TBD (Priya + Rohit)

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya, AE on the Veridian account. Quick intros?
[00:00:08] Lena Ortiz: Hi, Lena here, head of AI at Veridian Health. We're looking to move some clinical summarization workloads into production and wanted to understand the cost and observability story.
[00:00:18] Marcus Ellison: Marcus, platform eng. We're most interested in per-route cost attribution so we can charge teams back accurately.
[00:00:23] Priya Nair: Priya, security. SOC2 and encryption questions.
[00:00:27] Rohit Gupta: Rohit, SE from Redwood — I'll take you through the Console demo and how we surface per-route metrics.
[00:00:33] Maya Chen: Quick agenda: Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, cost breakdown, Optimize suggestions, then Q&A and next steps.

[00:02:05] Rohit Gupta: Opening the Console — top-left you can see org-level token consumption, cost over time. This is a synthetic org view but mirrors what we'd provision for you. The route map on the right shows active routes — each route corresponds to an API key + route config, so per-team chargebacks are straightforward.
[00:02:35] Marcus Ellison: When you say route, is that per endpoint path or per model? We have some teams that hit the same model with different prompts.
[00:02:42] Rohit Gupta: Good question. Routes are logical — you can map them to endpoint paths, service names, or tags. In the Console we show route-level metrics (requests, tokens in/out, p99 latency) and model attribution. So if two routes hit the same model, the cost and tokens show up on both routes separately.

[00:04:10] Rohit Gupta: Scrolling into a route: here's Route "clinical-summaries-v1" — timeframe last 30 days. You get calls-per-minute, tokens-per-call, CPU/GPU utilization on Dedicated, and cost-per-token breakdown. Notice the token distribution spike on Oct 4th which corresponds to a dataset onboarding.
[00:04:40] Sam Wu: The token distribution looks noisy — can we bucket by user or by prompt set?
[00:04:45] Rohit Gupta: Yes — you can apply filters (user_id header, team tag, request metadata). The Console also accepts custom attributes in headers which makes slicing simple.

[00:06:00] Lena Ortiz: On cost — what granularity is that? Per-token only or do you amortize GPU runtime / reserved capacity?
[00:06:08] Rohit Gupta: Both. For Hosted API we show unit cost per token derived from your pricing plan; for Dedicated we show amortized cost across GPUs (reserved monthly commit) plus per-instance overhead. The Console lets you view cost by route with a breakdown: model compute, storage (KV cache), network, and reserved capacity amortization.

[00:07:20] Rohit Gupta: Here's an example cost waterfall for a route: model inference tokens -> batching efficiency factor -> reserved GPU amortization -> cache hits deduction. We also surface wasted tokens and cold-start penalties.
[00:07:42] Marcus Ellison: Can you export per-route cost to our internal billing system? We want CSVs every day to push into Snowflake.
[00:07:48] Rohit Gupta: Absolutely — there's an export API and scheduled S3 exports. We can push daily CSVs with route_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_breakdown columns.

[00:09:10] Rohit Gupta: Switching to Optimize tab — this analyzes your recent workload and gives tuning suggestions: increase batching window for short-prompt routes, enable KV prefix caching for templates, recommend quantized model variants for latency-insensitive routes. Each suggestion shows estimated cost savings and potential latency delta.
[00:09:35] Sam Wu: What's the accuracy risk if we enable a 4-bit quantized profile? We care about clinical accuracy.
[00:09:42] Rohit Gupta: We flag routes where quality-sensitive prompts exist. For those we recommend running canary evaluations — Redwood Optimize can run prompt sets against the quantized variant and report ROUGE/BLEU differences and a small diff sample. We don't auto-flip anything; it's always a canary + human approval.

[00:11:05] Priya Nair: Security — where do logs and PII live? If we use Hosted, are transcripts stored, and can we bring our own KMS?
[00:11:14] Maya Chen: Short answer: Hosted stores request/response logs by default for 30 days for troubleshooting; we offer retention controls. For sensitive customers we have Dedicated and Private options with customer-managed KMS and no request persistence if configured.
[00:11:35] Rohit Gupta: In Private deployments we can disable retention, and we support HSM-based key management. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption with BYOK via supported KMS providers.

[00:12:50] Marcus Ellison: On Dedicated vs Hosted, how does the cost graph look? If we commit to Dedicated, how do we model break-even?
[00:12:58] Rohit Gupta: The Console has a Reserved vs On-demand calculator. You can input expected qps and model mix; it models monthly GPU costs, utilization, and gives projected per-token cost. For example, at 100k tokens/sec sustained, Dedicated often wins after three months depending on model size and utilization. We'll provide a TCO spreadsheet.

[00:15:10] Rohit Gupta: Back to per-route dashboards: you can set alerting rules — e.g., route cost exceeds $X/day, p99 latency > 400ms — and attach automated rollback/fallback policies to route configs.
[00:15:25] Lena Ortiz: Does rollback switch to a smaller model automatically?
[00:15:29] Rohit Gupta: Yes you can configure policy: fallback to cheaper/compressed variant or reduce max tokens. The Console also tracks degradation metrics post-rollout to validate impact.

[00:17:00] Rohit Gupta: Demoing the query inspector — select a single request and view full trace: token timeline, kernel selection, batching window, and cache hits. This is useful for debugging latency spikes.
[00:17:20] Marcus Ellison: Kernel selection — can we pin a kernel or force a path for reproducibility?
[00:17:25] Rohit Gupta: There are runtime flags in Dedicated/Private to pin kernels; in Hosted we select automatically but you can request a kernel pin with an enterprise support ticket for specific runs.

[00:19:10] Sam Wu: For per-team chargeback, what if a request is multi-tenant, e.g., a pipeline that triggers several routes?
[00:19:20] Rohit Gupta: The Console supports composite reports — you can define a billing group that aggregates multiple routes and then generate a single invoice line. We also support per-request metadata so you can tag downstream costs to the original caller.

[00:21:00] Rohit Gupta: Now showing the Cost Explorer — you can slice by model, route, team, and by tag. Here's an example where we attribute 60% of spend to three heavy routes. We surface a heatmap for token cost by hour so you can find batch windows.
[00:21:30] Lena Ortiz: Any suggestion to reduce cost for our nightly batch jobs?
[00:21:35] Rohit Gupta: Yes — move the nightly jobs to a quantized variant or run them on Dedicated off-peak capacity; enable larger batching window and persistent KV cache to avoid repeated context tokens. Optimize will estimate savings.

[00:23:00] Priya Nair: Auditability — do you keep immutable logs for compliance? We need to show access to keys and who ran what.
[00:23:10] Rohit Gupta: We provide audit logs with read-only retention options, plus RBAC tied to SSO. For Dedicated/Private, you can forward logs to your SIEM.

[00:25:50] Marcus Ellison: How long does it take to provision Dedicated capacity if we decide to commit?
[00:25:56] Maya Chen: Typical lead time is 4-8 weeks depending on hardware and region specifics. There are fast-track options for preferred customers.

[00:27:15] Rohit Gupta: Showing the Route comparison view — you can compare token efficiency across models and prompt templates. We also surface suggested prompt edits that reduce tokens without changing intent — it's a mix of automated n-gram trimming suggestions and manual notes.
[00:27:40] Sam Wu: Could be handy — our prompts are pretty verbose.

[00:29:00] Rohit Gupta: Quick note on caching: KV prefix caching helps a lot for templated clinical notes. If you have common prefixes, we can cache the key-value outputs and reduce model runs significantly. Cache hit rates show directly in the route metrics.

[00:30:20] Priya Nair: If we enable caching, where does the cache live? Is it encrypted?
[00:30:25] Rohit Gupta: Cache can be local to the serving runtime or a managed Redis; in Private deployments it lives in your VPC and is encrypted with your keys. In Hosted it's encrypted at rest; you can opt for customer-managed encryption for additional controls.

[00:32:00] Rohit Gupta: Walkthrough of policy-based routing — you can route a request based on latency budget, cost cap, or region. Example: route clinical-summaries requests to Dedicated in us-west for production, fallback to Hosted in us-east if capacity constrained.
[00:32:20] Marcus Ellison: Does the fallback keep the same model version?
[00:32:24] Rohit Gupta: We try to use compatible model variants; if exact model isn't available, we can map to a closest equivalent and surface a compatibility score.

[00:34:10] Maya Chen: Quick commercial note — pricing for Hosted will be token-based; Dedicated is reserved GPU with monthly commit. We will send you a TCO that models both.

[00:35:30] Lena Ortiz: Can you show an example of an Optimize recommendation and the confidence estimate?
[00:35:38] Rohit Gupta: Sure — here's an Optimize card recommending 2x batching for route X with estimated 30% cost reduction and estimated p99 increase of 40ms. Confidence is based on historical variance; we show a low/med/high label and the sample size used to compute the estimate.

[00:36:50] Sam Wu: For the canary evaluations you mentioned, do you run them on our data? Any privacy issues?
[00:36:59] Rohit Gupta: We can run canaries on synthetic or mirrored traffic—mirrored traffic is redacted and you control what we keep. For security-sensitive customers we recommend Private deployment or a bounded dedicated trial where everything stays in your VPC.

[00:38:40] Priya Nair: Ok important — what certifications do you have? SOC 2 Type II? ISO?
[00:38:46] Maya Chen: We maintain SOC 2 Type II and are pursuing ISO 27001 in the next cycle. We'll share the security pack and cert copies.

[00:40:00] Rohit Gupta: Back to routing — you can also do cost-aware routing: assign a cost budget per route and the system dynamically selects the cheapest compatible variant under the budget. Very useful for dev vs prod separation.

[00:41:30] Marcus Ellison: Can we tag routes by project and then generate monthly reports per project?
[00:41:34] Rohit Gupta: Yep — tagging and project-level rollups are standard. You can also define billing owners so notifications go to the right teams.

[00:43:10] Maya Chen: Recap of agreed next steps: we'll send the TCO spreadsheet and a sample per-route CSV, Rohit will set up a 48-hour perf run against a dev model, and we'll schedule a security deep-dive with Priya.
[00:43:35] Lena Ortiz: Sounds good — can you include recommendations for quick wins? We're hoping for a 15-20% immediate cost reduction.
[00:43:42] Rohit Gupta: Yes — we'll highlight quick wins: enable KV caching for templated routes, increase batching for nightly jobs, and run quantized run for non-clinical batch tasks.

[00:45:20] Priya Nair: Please send the security pack before the deep-dive so we can prepare questions.
[00:45:25] Maya Chen: Will do.

[00:46:00] Maya Chen: Any other questions?
[00:46:05] Sam Wu: No, thanks — this was helpful.
[00:46:10] Marcus Ellison: Good session.
[00:46:15] Lena Ortiz: Thanks everyone.
[00:47:30] Rohit Gupta: Thanks — we'll follow up with notes and the sheet.

End of transcript.
